WinkBeds · Convert exp 100350628 · QA 2026-09-29

WIN276 Other: Targeted Offer V2

Based on WIN257 cart-modal upgrade Targeting sitewide, all users, custom trigger Browsers Chrome + Safari, desktop + mobile
Not ready to launch

The modal, copy and upgrade flow work, and every exclusion rule behaves correctly. But the new Cohort 2 audience, the point of this test, cannot be reached by real visitors (BUG-01). Even when it is armed, it is lost as soon as the user scrolls (BUG-02). As built, the Variation would run as a copy of Control with a 5-second delay.

How it was tested

Code read directly from the live Convert bundle: cre-t-276-deployment (100350629), creT276Activation (100350630), and the Control and Variation of 100350628. Each case seeds the relevant state (checkout cookie, cre276_cart_added_ts, cre276_last_active_ts set 2h in the past, real cart items), then opens the QA force link in a fresh browser context. Cart writes are real, on winkbeds.com, in throwaway sessions; no orders were placed.

Bugs

criticalBUG-01

Cohort 2 can never qualify: real Add to Cart is not tracked

cre-t-276-deployment · trackCartAdd()

What happens
The deployment wraps window.fetch and only reacts to URLs containing /cart/add. On winkbeds.com both the shop-winkbed Buy Box and the product page add to cart with POST /cart/update.js ({"updates":{"<variant>":1}}). cre276_cart_added_ts is never written, so no real visitor can ever enter Cohort 2 and the Variation behaves exactly like Control.
Evidence
TC-11 fails on all 4 browsers. The request log shows only /cart/update.js; the cart holds “The LUXURY FIRM WinkBed - Queen x1” and the flag is null.
Suggested fix
Don’t depend on the request shape. On each page load, read /cart.js; if an eligible WinkBed is in the cart and no flag exists, write the timestamp. At minimum also match /cart/update and /cart/change.
criticalBUG-02

Any scroll, mouse move or key press on the return visit cancels the “new session”

deployment trackActivity() + activation qualifiesForCohort2() + variation exclusionLogicsApply()

What happens
The first interaction writes cre276_last_active_ts = now immediately (throttle starts at 0). The activation checks isNewSession() 3s later, and the Variation checks it again after a further 5s. A returning visitor who scrolls or moves the mouse in those first ~8s is no longer “new”. Either the experiment never triggers, or the user is bucketed into the Variation and never sees the modal, which dilutes the Variation’s results.
Evidence
TC-06 fails on all 4 browsers. Chrome: bucketed into Variation, no modal, last_active 20s old. Safari / mobile: experiment not triggered at all.
Suggested fix
Decide “returning session” once, at deployment init, before the activity listeners are attached (e.g. store sessionStorage.cre276_return_session = 1). The activation and Variation should read that snapshot, not recompute from the live timestamp.
highBUG-03

Control and Variation show Cohort 1 at different times; Cohort 2 is later than 5s

variation init() · setTimeout(…, 5000)

What happens
The Variation waits an extra 5s for every user, Cohort 1 included, while the Control shows the modal as soon as the experiment runs. The same audience gets a different experience in each arm, and Variation users who leave within those 5s never see the offer. Cohort 2 also lands at 3s (activation) + 5s (variation) + load time, well past the 5s in the brief.
Evidence
Cohort 1, seconds from navigation start. Chrome: Control 6.5 / Variation 11.1. Mobile Chrome: 6.0 / 11.5. Safari Desktop (from DOMContentLoaded): 6.3 / 9.8. Cohort 2: Chrome 11.3s, Mobile Chrome 11.5s, Safari 9.8s, Mobile Safari 20.7s.
Suggested fix
Apply the 5s wait only to Cohort 2, and count it from page load. Leave Cohort 1 timing identical to Control.
highBUG-04

Cohort 2 modal re-appears on every later return session

deployment · cre276_cart_added_ts is never cleared

What happens
Once shown, nothing marks the offer as seen. Every time the user comes back after 1h+ with the same cart, the Variation shows the modal again. Control consumes its Cohort 1 cookie after one showing, so the arms also differ in how often the offer is seen.
Evidence
TC-15 fails on all 4 browsers (second showing: Chrome 10.8s, Safari 13.9s, Mobile Chrome 7.7s, Mobile Safari 19.9s).
Suggested fix
Set a persistent “shown” flag when the Cohort 2 modal is displayed, or clear the cart-added flag, and check it in the activation.
highBUG-05

A user who returns to an idle open tab is never treated as a new session

activation · evaluation runs only on page load / bfcache pageshow

What happens
The agreed definition says any interaction after 1h+ of inactivity counts as a return and re-triggers evaluation. The code never re-evaluates in an open tab, and the first interaction resets the timer, so the next page view isn’t “new” either.
Evidence
Code review. Follows from the same timestamp handling as BUG-02.
Suggested fix
In markActive(), if the previous timestamp is 1h+ old, flag a return session and re-run the activation check before overwriting it.
highBUG-06

Go-live: WIN257 is live as a 100% deployment and will stack with WIN276

Convert deploy 100350512 (cre-t-257), audience “campaign does NOT contain Cro276mode”

What happens
WIN257’s modal currently runs for all real traffic, and is excluded only for this QA’s Cro276mode param. When WIN276’s QA audience is removed, checkout abandoners will get both the WIN257 modal and the WIN276 modal unless 100350512 is paused.
Evidence
Convert project bundle, 2026-09-29.
Suggested fix
Pause 100350512 (and the WIN257 global activation) at WIN276 launch.
mediumBUG-07

Cohort 1 is looser than WIN257’s definition

activation qualifiesForCohort1()

What happens
WIN257 requires the checkout cookie and Shopify’s __ui … checkoutSessionIdentifier. WIN276 dropped the second check, so a mousedown on “Continue to checkout” alone qualifies, even if checkout never loaded. The brief says Control should use the existing WIN257 targeting.
Evidence
Code comparison with the live WIN257 activation in the Convert global JS.
Suggested fix
Restore hasCheckoutSessionIdentifier() in the Cohort 1 check.
mediumBUG-08

Checkout visitors can later fall into Cohort 2

deployment · cre_276_checkout_visited is a session cookie

What happens
The “previously reached Checkout” exclusion reads a session cookie that is deleted as soon as the Cohort 1 modal is shown, and is also lost when the browser closes. After either, a checkout visitor with the cart flag set qualifies as Cohort 2 (Variation only), so the cohorts aren’t mutually exclusive as required.
Evidence
Code review. Masked today by BUG-01; becomes live once BUG-01 is fixed.
Suggested fix
Also store a persistent localStorage.cre276_checkout_reached and exclude it from Cohort 2.
lowBUG-09

Stale WIN257 goal fired from both arms

control + variation modalInsertion()

What happens
triggerConversion "100334268" is WIN257’s goal (comment still reads “update to WIN276 goal ID”). It isn’t attached to experiment 100350628. The real WIN276 goal 100334580 is also fired, so tracking works, but the stray call should go.
Evidence
Convert bundle goal list for 100350628: 100321041, 100327778, 100324238, 100334580, 100334581.
Suggested fix
Remove the 100334268 push.

Working as specified

  • One combined trigger. Convert buckets Cohort 1 and Cohort 2 users into both arms (TC-05: Cohort 2 in Control enters the test with no modal).
  • Exclusions: same session, Cooling Cover already in cart, empty cart, no signals (TC-07 to TC-10).
  • Cart check now requires quantity 1, fixing WIN257’s old qty-2 issue.
  • CTA replaces the mattress with the “with Frost Cooling Cover” variant and lands on checkout with FROST8UYR31 (−$125) applied, on all 4 browsers.
  • Copy matches WIN257. Page blurs behind the modal; close icon dismisses.

Agreed limitations (not logged as bugs)

  • Purchase and “already claimed” are not tracked.
  • Checkout visits count only via clicks on a[href="/checkout"]; direct URL or Shop Pay / express buttons are missed.
  • Carry-over from WIN257, not re-tested: cart is emptied before the new variant is found, redirect fires even if the swap fails, “winkbed” substring match (Kids / Blue Collection), no double-click guard, limited keyboard support.
  • Mobile Safari timings (16–22s) are inflated by slow WebKit loading of this site; the fixed +5s in the code is the defect, not the absolute number.
